items.title: Coinbase Gives EU Users USDT Deadline
points: Coinbase is requiring EU users to convert, transfer, or withdraw USDT (Tether stablecoin, a cryptocurrency pegged 1:1 to the US dollar) holdings by a specified deadline.
Move appears driven by EU regulatory requirements around stablecoin offerings and exchange compliance.
Users who miss the deadline risk forced conversion or account restrictions on their USDT holdings.
Signals major exchanges beginning to comply with stricter EU digital finance rules, potentially affecting other stablecoins in the region.

items.title: Circle Revenue At Risk From AI Displacement
points: Mizuho downgraded Circle to Underperform with a $43 price target, a 46% downside from $79.84, citing AI personal assistants steering users to higher-yielding alternatives to USDC (a US dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle).

Modeling shows USDC market cap could shrink $4B-$9B with reserve revenue falling 10-20% as AI agents redirect users from Circle's non-yielding platform (17% of USDC) to Coinbase (30%) or other platforms (53%).
Under faster AI adoption, Mizuho projects 2027 USDC average supply of $101B (down from $108B), reserve revenue of $4.1B (down 5%), and adjusted EBITDA of $603M (down 5%).

items.title: BNB Chain Builds Parallel High-Speed Layer 1
points: Binance founder CZ confirmed a new EVM-compatible (Ethereum Virtual Machine-compatible, meaning it can run Ethereum-style smart contracts) parallel Layer 1 blockchain for BNB Chain targeting high-frequency trading.
The chain will run parallel to BNB Smart Chain, connected via a native bridge, and use BNB for gas, staking (delegated proof-of-stake securing the network), and governance.
Technical specs target 200-millisecond block times and 20-millisecond pre-confirmations (advance commitment to transaction ordering before finality).

Planned features include native account abstraction (simplified transaction handling without requiring traditional accounts) and onchain privacy pools; internal devnet is live, with public testnet targeted late 2026 and mainnet early 2027.

items.title: Onchain Options Market Primed for Retail Growth
points: Onchain options currently represent 6.9% of Deribit volume, with infrastructure now mature—regulation, market-making, and RFQ (request-for-quote) systems resolved—leaving retail distribution as the primary growth barrier.

Retail drove growth in comparable markets: US stock options volume tripled from 4.19B to 15.2B contracts (2017-2025) after Robinhood removed commissions, while 0DTE (same-day expiration) options grew from 5% to 60% of S&P 500 index volume in a decade.

Korea case illustrates offshore spillover: regulations cut domestic retail participation 85%, but Korean retail now trades 3.6x more volume offshore, positioning onchain venues to capture demand displaced from over-regulated markets.

items.title: Keystone Hardware Wallet Manufacturing Breach
points: An attacker pivoted from a compromised third-party monitoring tool to access 25,964 buyer records, 12,873 incomplete checkouts, and the WebAuth device authentication key burned into hardware during manufacturing.

The compromised key enables production of counterfeit Keystones that pass authentication checks; user assets, recovery phrases, and private keys are unaffected, but device genuineness verification is now compromised.

Keystone is destroying all 18,835 devices in inventory, suspending unshipped orders, and halting production under the compromised key; a Shopify data-erasure tool failure caused customer records to be retained beyond the 180-day policy, widening the exposure window.

items.title: Fireblocks Denies Visa Rumors, Confirms Layoffs
points: Fireblocks denied Visa acquisition rumors then confirmed a 7% workforce cut, marking its third layoff round.
This comes despite Fireblocks having raised $1.04B in total capital, raising questions about institutional crypto infrastructure valuations.
